name: Pork Chops with Apple Sauce
steps: Peel, core and chop the apples. Put them in a small saucepan with the brown sugar, ground cinnamon, apple cider vinegar and 2 tbsp of water. Cover and simmer over low heat for 15-20 minutes, until the apples collapse, then mash to a chunky sauce and stir in 20 g of the butter. Keep warm.

Meanwhile, peel the potatoes, cut them into even chunks and boil in a large pot of salted water for 15-20 minutes, until tender when pierced with a knife. Drain as soon as they're tender, return to the hot pot and cover with the lid to keep warm.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Pat the pork chops dry, then rub them all over with the dijon mustard, a good pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over high heat. Sear the chops for 2-3 minutes on each side, until deeply golden.

Transfer the pan to the oven and roast the chops for 5-10 minutes depending on thickness, until just cooked through with a hint of blush at the centre (63°C on a meat thermometer). Rest on a warm plate for 5 minutes.
While the chops rest, mash the drained potatoes with the remaining 40 g of butter and the full cream milk. Season with salt and pepper.
Boil or steam the green beans for 3-4 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Season with a pinch of salt.
Serve the chops on the mash with the green beans alongside, spooning the warm apple sauce generously over the pork.
